accepted.question_text: Let E be a Banach space, and call a nonzero subspace E1 of E prime when there is no proper subspace E2 of E such that E is the orthogonal direct sum of E1 and E2. Every finite-dimensional Banach space can be decomposed as an orthogonal direct sum of prime subspaces. Is such a prime decomposition unique in any natural sense?
accepted.context_brief: uniqueness of prime decompositions in p-adic Banach spaces

evidence.quote: A non-zero subspace \(E\_ 1\) of a Banach space \(E\) is said to be prime if there is no proper subspace \(E\_ 2\) of \(E\) such that \(E\) is the orthogonal direct sum of \(E\_ 1\) and \(E\_ 2\). Every finite-dimensional Banach space can be decomposed as an orthogonal direct sum of prime subspaces. Is the prime decomposition unique in a natural sense?

accepted.question_text: For the \(\ell^1\) space considered in this p-adic functional-analysis setting, is \(\ell^1\) ultrametrizable? The same source records that this question was solved negatively when the base field is non-trivially valued.

evidence.quote: One of the problems posed in this paper is the following: Is \(\ell^ 1\)- ultrametrizable? This has been solved by J. M. Bayod negatively when the base field is non-trivially valued, and this has appeared in the same volume in which this paper under review has appeared.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The authors state that it is not known whether every cartesian normed space is Hilbertian.

evidence.quote: A \(p\)-adic normed space is called Hilbertian if every one-dimensional linear subspace has an orthogonal complement. The authors state that it is not known whether every cartesian normed space is Hilbertian.
